text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele gives an extended interview on his views on the sea border row with Lithuania.
- Lithuania's youngest finance minister, 28-year-old Rolandas Matiliauskas, said that he will pay much attention to the banking sector and follow the economic programm of the Homeland Union.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas departed to Lisbon Sunday to participate in the OSCE summit. Brazauskas is expected to meet Belarus leader Alexander Lukashenko.

- Foreign capital is becoming interested in our country, said the director general of Lithuania's Investment agency, Algis Avizhienis. Investments in 1995 were $50 million and are this year estimated at $100 million.

- The council of the Centre Union party decided Sunday to back taking part in the new government of Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius, who last week suggested that the party take the posts of construction and urban and environment protection minister.

- Russian LUKoil and Saudi Arabian ARA Group officially refused to buy Butinges Terminal shares. Omegon Petroleum Products, an off-shore company, would like buy 33 percent, Preussag from Germany 30 percent and Fluor Daniel of the USA five percent of Butinge terminal.
- Foreign debt increased by 1.3 times during the first 10 months of this year and on November 1 was 3.668 billion litas ($917 million).
- From today, trading on the stock exchange will be held every day as group A shares will will be traded on Monday, Wednesday and Friday and the rest of the market on Tuesday and Thursday.
